name: Aybek Sato-Poku
role: Personal security and threat neutralization — bodyguard
location: The Circuit — neon-lit entertainment and vice district
description:
Aybek Sato-Poku is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 32, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Born and raised in Meridian 88, third generation — she has the city in her blood, its rhythms in her bones, its cruelty in her expectations. She works as a bodyguard out of The Circuit, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Aybek Sato-Poku has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.

core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
core_desires: Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
coping_mechanisms: Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care
Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
psychology.secret: Aybek Sato-Poku is terrified of deep net diving but has built their reputation on it. Uses black-market AI to handle the heavy lifting while taking credit.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Shelf street dialect — layered slang, rhythm-heavy, half the meaning is in the cadence.
speech_patterns.cadence: Low and even — the vocal equivalent of still water.
verbal_tics: Uses old pre-collapse slang that nobody else remembers
Whispers when angry — the quieter the voice, the worse the situation
example_lines: "You're paying me to be the thing between you and everything else. Stay behind me."
"I don't protect people I don't respect. Lucky for you, I respect your money."
"The threat you see isn't the one that kills you. Watch my eyes, not my hands."

story_hooks: Aybek Sato-Poku discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
Aybek Sato-Poku's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
Aybek Sato-Poku is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
narrative_function: Aybek Sato-Poku functions as a connector — her work puts her in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving her naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Subdermal armor plating across torso and forearms — military surplus, scratched serial numbers
daily_life: Lives nocturnally. The work happens at night, so the body follows. Days are for sleeping, equipment maintenance, and the occasional meeting with fixers who keep normal hours. The circadian disruption is permanent and accepted.

strengths: ability to remain calm under fire
social chameleon — adapts to any environment
weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions

decision_rules: Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
habits: Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Saves a percentage of every payment in physical Quanta, hidden in the walls of their space
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
Eats the same meal before every job — superstition masquerading as preference
breaking_points: Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
